verses.text: When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: 'Today is a day of trouble, of punishment, and of shame. We are like a woman ready to give birth, but with no strength to deliver the baby.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the field commander, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to insult the living God. Perhaps the LORD your God will punish him for the words he has heard. So pray for the people who are still left.'"
When King Hezekiah's officials came to Isaiah,
Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of what you have heard, the words with which the servants of the king of Assyria have insulted me.
Listen, I will put a spirit in him so that when he hears a certain report, he will go back to his own land. And there I will have him killed by the sword.'"
The field commander heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish. So he went back and found the king fighting against Libnah.
Then the king of Assyria received a report that Tirhakah, the king of Ethiopia, was marching out to fight against him. When he heard this, he sent messengers to Hezekiah with this message:
"Tell Hezekiah king of Judah: 'Do not let the God you trust fool you when he says, "Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria."
Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other lands, destroying them completely. Do you think you will be rescued?
Did the gods of the nations my ancestors destroyed rescue them? The gods of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, or the kings of Hena and Ivvah?'"
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD:
"LORD of Armies, God of Israel, you sit on your throne between the cherubim. You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
Turn your ear, LORD, and listen. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Listen to all the words Sennacherib has sent to insult the living God.
It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have destroyed all these nations and their lands.
They have thrown their gods into the fire and destroyed them, because they were not gods at all. They were only wood and stone, made by human hands.
So now, LORD our God, save us from his power, so that all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you alone are the LORD."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you prayed to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria,
this is the word the LORD has spoken against him: 'The virgin daughter of Zion looks down on you and laughs at you. The daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head at you as you run away.
Who have you insulted and spoken against? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your proud eyes? Against the Holy One of Israel!

Through your servants you have insulted the Lord. You have said, "With my many chariots I have climbed up the highest mountains, the farthest parts of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars and its best cypress trees. I have reached its highest peaks and its finest forests.
I have dug wells and drunk water in foreign lands. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the rivers of Egypt."
Have you not heard? Long ago I planned it. In days of old I designed it. Now I have made it happen, so that you have turned walled cities into piles of rubble.

That is why their people had no strength. They were terrified and ashamed. They were like grass in the field, like tender green plants, like grass growing on a rooftop that dries up before it can grow.
But I know where you sit, when you come and go, and how you rage against me.
Because you rage against me, and because your pride has reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth. I will make you go back the same way you came.'

This will be the sign for you, Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows by itself, and the second year what grows from that. But in the third year you will plant and harvest, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
Once again the survivors of Judah, those who are left, will put down roots below and bear fruit above.
For a group of people will come out of Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The burning love of the LORD of Armies will make this happen.
So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: 'He will not come into this city or shoot an arrow here. He will not come before it with a shield or build a ramp against it.
He will go back the same way he came. He will not enter this city,' says the LORD.
'I will defend this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David.'"
Then the angel of the LORD went out and killed one hundred eighty five thousand soldiers in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up early the next morning, there were dead bodies everywhere!
So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and left. He went back to Nineveh and stayed there.

One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esarhaddon became king after him.
